title: Integration discovery - Gravitas Retail
summary: Intro discovery focused on integration options for Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Customer requirements: low-latency checkout assistant, embeddings for product search, LangChain/LlamaIndex support, strict data residency and KMS, SSO. Action items: send SDK examples, dedicated sizing, security docs, schedule POC benchmark.
action_items: Jordan Lee: Share Redwood SDK quickstart repo + LangChain/LlamaIndex example (due 2028-03-17)
Priya Nair: Provide dedicated sizing estimate and pricing spreadsheet (due 2028-03-18)
Sofia Alvarez: Send sample prompt set and perf targets for checkout assistant (due 2028-03-16)
next_steps: Redwood to send SDK examples and security docs
Schedule 1-hr POC kickoff next week to run latency benchmark on 1k sample queries
Customer to confirm data residency region and KMS preferences
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we should have about 45 minutes. I'm Jordan Lee, AE at Redwood.
[00:06] Maya: Hi Jordan, thanks, I'm Maya CTO at Gravitas. We have Liam and Sofia with us.
[00:12] Liam: Afternoon.
[00:14] Jordan: Great, quick agenda 	6 integration paths (SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex), hosted vs dedicated vs private, quotas/rate limits, observability and next steps. Priya from our SE team will take the deep part.
[00:24] Priya: Hi all, quick follow, can you tell us your primary usage patterns? Latency needs, throughput, and any compliance constraints?
[00:31] Sofia: Sure 	6 two main things: a checkout assistant that needs sub-150ms p95 for short prompts, and a product search embeddings pipeline, batch embeddings near-real-time. Also we have strict PCI adjacency and want customer data never leaving our VPC if possible.
[00:46] Priya: Understood. For the checkout assistant, people typically look at hosted for easiest onboarding, dedicated if you need predictable throughput, and private/VPC for strict network controls. Small note 	6 hosted can do VPC egress via private link in some regions, but if you require full on-prem air-gapped we look at Private.
[01:02] Maya: Do you have examples for LangChain or LlamaIndex? Our search team uses LlamaIndex heavily.
[01:07] Jordan: Yes, we have Python and Node SDKs, plus pre-built connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex. We'll send a repo link after the call. The connector maps streaming tokens, embeddings and has guides for retry/backoff.
[01:17] Sofia: Any adapter for gateway/proxy? We route all requests through our internal API gateway and need to surface traces.
[01:22] Priya: You can put Redwood behind your gateway 	6 our SDK supports API keys and short-lived tokens. We also support a proxy-mode where requests are routed through a customer gateway; trace ids can be passed via headers and we ingest them into our console traces. There's slight overhead if you run an extra proxy but it's common.
[01:39] Liam: Rate limits 	6 how granular are quotas? Per-key? Per-organization? We need bursty traffic during promotions.
[01:46] Priya: Quotas are configurable: per API key, per org, and per-route. For Dedicated we can provision burst capacity and configure autoscaling policies. Hosted has standard tier limits but we can carve out custom limits on enterprise plans. We'll include quota examples in the doc.
[02:01] Maya: Security 	6 SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS. We use AWS KMS for key management and require audit logs forwarded to our SIEM.
[02:09] Jordan: We are SOC2 Type II; we integrate with customer KMS in Dedicated and Private modes. For hosted we offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options via KMS in supported regions. Audit logs can be streamed 	6 we have hooks to send to CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Splunk.
[02:23] Sofia: Good. For the POC we'd like to run a benchmark of 1k checkout prompts from our dataset 	6 can Redwood run that inside a private sandbox?
[02:31] Priya: For repeatable benchmarks we typically spin up a dedicated cluster pinned to a model variant. If you need to keep data in your VPC we can run Private or Dedicated with VPC peering. Either way we'll capture latency distributions, token counts, and resource usage.
[02:45] Liam: How about LangChain 	6 does your connector support chains with tool calls and function calling? We rely on structured output and tool integrations.
[02:53] Priya: Yes 	6 our SDK supports function calling and structured output. LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors can annotate outputs and map tool calls back to your orchestration. There's a small caveat about streaming function call tokens 	6 we have examples.
[03:05] Maya: Any gotchas with LlamaIndex and embeddings? We use 1536-d embeddings and sometimes store vectors in our managed Pinecone.
[03:12] Priya: Works fine. We export embeddings in standard float32/float16 or quantized formats. For heavy embedding loads we recommend batch endpoints and asynchronous jobs to smooth throughput and reduce cost. We'll include batching recommendations.
[03:26] Jordan: Pricing touch 	6 hosted per-token + embedding units; Dedicated is committed monthly capacity, and Private has platform fee + support. We'll send a high level pricing sheet after.
[03:36] Liam: For Dedicated sizing 	6 what info do you need?
[03:39] Priya: Typical inputs: expected peak RPS, average tokens per request, embedding QPS, latency SLO, and concurrency. We'll take your 1k prompt test and size accordingly.
[03:48] Maya: Observability 	6 we need per-request traces, token-level cost breakdown, and model-level dashboards.
[03:54] Priya: Redwood Console provides per-route latency, token billing, trace IDs, and error analysis. You can also pull metrics via API or push to your Prometheus stack. We'll share sample dashboards.
[04:06] Sofia: Any pitfalls with proxy headers and preserving client IPs for rate limiting?
[04:10] Priya: If you terminate TLS at your gateway you can forward X-Forwarded-For and we can map to org keys. Rate limiting granularity can use header-based tags. We'll document recommended header patterns.
[04:21] Jordan: Quick Q 	6 are there competitors you're evaluating?
[04:24] Maya: We're also looking at OpenAI for hosted and Lambda Labs for on-prem. Anthropic for safety features.
[04:30] Jordan: Understood. We differentiate on predictable latency and deployment choices.
[04:34] Maya: Timeline 	6 we'd like to run a POC in the next 2 weeks and decide by end of month.
[04:39] Jordan: Sounds good. We'll aim to have the POC kickoff scheduled within 7 days.
[04:44] Priya: I'll draft a POC plan 	6 endpoints, sample dataset, metrics we will collect (p95 latency, throughput, token cost, memory).
[04:52] Sofia: For the POC, we require SSO access and a temporary dedicated cluster. Also need security questionnaires answered.
[04:59] Jordan: We'll send the security pack and SSO setup steps; Priya will include the POC runbook.
[05:05] Maya: Perfect.
[05:07] Jordan: Recap and next steps 	6 Jordan to send SDK repos and pricing, Priya to send sizing + POC plan, Sofia to send sample prompt set. We'll target POC kickoff next Wednesday. Any final Qs?
[05:19] Liam: None from me.
[05:20] Maya: No, thanks.
[05:22] Jordan: Thanks all, talk soon.
file_notes: Transcript contains typical ASR errors and occasional speaker label slips; timestamps rough every 20-60s. Refs to docs/repos will be sent as links in next steps.
